A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BiM-VFI and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables and appendices. Corresponding content can be reliably matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original interpolation benchmarks, component ablations, qualitative comparisons and a user study with 21 participants.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds computational-cost measurements and visual comparisons with and without CAUN.

M1.justification: The described BiM representation, BiMFN, CAUN, shared-weight teacher/student training and uniform-motion inference remain unchanged. The loss functions move from Section 3.5 to Appendix A.3 without substantive modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use Vimeo90K triplet/septuplet, SNU-FILM, SNU-FILM-arb and XTest, including fixed-time and arbitrary-time interpolation. The added profiling and CAUN examples do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds an efficiency comparison involving GIMM-VFI-R, EMA-VFI, UPR and AMT. GIMM-VFI-R was not an evaluated comparator in v1. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables and user study is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new appendix analyses introduce component profiling at 256×256 and runtime comparisons on an A100 GPU at 1280×768. Original training and benchmark settings are retained, including Table 5's FLOP measurements at 1280×720.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a visual CAUN ablation examining preservation of toes and windmill-blade boundaries, with reconstructed images and flow visualizations. This supplements the existing numerical CAUN ablation; the other ablations and uniform-motion case study remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The user study retains the same 21 participants, nine videos and preference-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the 61% user preference remain unchanged. New results include 78.49 GFLOPs at 256×256, 151-ms inference at 1280×768 and CAUN visual findings. The newly reported 6.88M parameter total conflicts with the retained 6.0M in Table 5.

T1.justification: The BiM definitions, synthesis and loss equations, and Theorem 1 with its geometric proof are retained. The proof moves from Appendix A.3 to A.5; equation renumbering and a flow-subscript typo correction do not change the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same methodological contributions and perceptual-quality claims, including the headline 26% LPIPS and 45% STLPIPS improvements. Removing the introduction's contribution bullets does not remove their substantive claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 now frames uniform-motion inference as a limitation shared by all VFI methods and attributes the tendency to training data dominated by uniform motion. v1 instead emphasized a data-driven tendency supporting the assumption's validity. Figure 6 supplying the evidence is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies training durations of 2.5 versus four days on four A100 GPUs and identifies the hardware and image dimensions for runtime profiling. Existing augmentation, optimizer, batch size, epochs, pyramid settings and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The same 45 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained, including positioning against distance indexing and pretrained-flow supervision. The added efficiency comparison does not revise the stated novelty or research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 removes the contribution bullets, moves losses and implementation details into the appendix, places references before the supplement, and adds acknowledgments and an appendix overview. Section 4.5 and author information receive localized edits; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds two unnumbered complexity tables and an unnumbered CAUN comparison panel. Existing numbered figures and tables are retained with layout adjustments and relocation. Table 3's 'w/o GUN' label is corrected to 'w/o CAUN'.

improvement.justification: The added component costs, GPU timing information and CAUN visual ablation make efficiency and module behavior easier to assess. The gain is limited: benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the new 6.88M parameter count conflicts with Table 5's retained 6.0M. The broader uniform-motion interpretation also relies on unchanged evidence.
